description: 2006 is the Year of the Fire Dog in the Chinese zodiac, from January 29, 2006 to February 17, 2007. Personality, Lunar New Year dates and numerology.
answer: In Chinese astrology, 2006 is the Year of the Fire Dog, a Yang year. It began at Lunar New Year on January 29, 2006 and ended on February 17, 2007, so people born in 2006 before Jan 29 belong to the Wood Rooster year.

sections.heading: 2006 Lunar New Year: start and end dates
paragraphs: Lunar New Year opened the Fire Dog year on January 29, 2006, and the year ran to February 17, 2007. So a birth date of Jan 29, 2006 or later counts as Fire Dog, and so do early 2007 birthdays through Feb 17; births in 2006 before Jan 29 still belong to the Wood Rooster. That moving boundary comes from the lunisolar calendar, in which the new year starts with the second new moon after the winter solstice in most years, so its Gregorian date shifts by up to a month from one year to the next. Look sixty years either side and the pairing repeats: 1946 are Fire Dog years too. That Sunday new year arrived with the Sun in Aquarius in the Western zodiac.

sections.heading: What the Fire Dog is like
paragraphs: In a Fire Dog year, the Dog's sense of duty gains passion and confidence. Classical readings picture people born now as charismatic, outspoken and quick to stand up against unfairness. Fire feeding Earth gives them stamina. Choosing battles wisely, pausing before reacting and extending grace to those who disappoint them are the suggestions readings commonly make. Their honesty, when kind, is a rare and valuable gift.

Belonging to the south and to the height of summer, Fire brings brightness, drive and visibility to any sign it colours. Classical texts connect it with enthusiasm, leadership and the urge to be seen and to make an impression. A Fire stem tends to make an animal more expressive, more daring and more openly emotional than its usual reputation suggests. People born in Fire years are often described as inspiring company and natural motivators. The caution most readings attach is a short fuse and a difficulty with slow seasons, when steady effort matters more than spark and the reward is a long way off.

sections.heading: 2006 in the animal cycle and in numerology
paragraphs: In numerology the digits reduce to 8, associated with ambition, authority and material results, so an 8 year is described in terms of effort and reward. The digits of 2006 add up to 8. The Dog holds the eleventh place among the twelve animals and its fixed element is Earth. Set beside the year's Fire stem, fire generates Earth, which readings use to describe how settled or stretched the combination feels. The year before was the Wood Rooster and the year after is the Fire Pig.

Chinese almanacs name 2006 Bing-Xu, pairing the Fire stem Bing with the branch Xu. Both are Yang, as stem and branch always share a polarity, so of the hundred and twenty possible pairings only sixty ever occur, and each one names a single year in every cycle.

faq.question: What Chinese zodiac is 2006?
faq.answer: 2006 is the Year of the Fire Dog. It started on January 29, 2006 and ended on February 17, 2007.

faq.question: What if I was born in January or February 2006?
faq.answer: Check the date against Jan 29. Born before January 29, 2006, you are a Wood Rooster; born on or after it, you are a Fire Dog.

faq.question: What element is 2006 in the Chinese zodiac?
faq.answer: Fire, a Yang year. The Dog's own fixed element is Earth; the year element changes every two years, while the fixed element stays with the animal.

faq.question: What is the traditional Chinese name for 2006?
faq.answer: Bing-Xu. The first part is the heavenly stem, which carries the year's element and polarity; the second is the earthly branch, which carries the animal. Almanacs, calendars and Four Pillars charts identify years this way rather than by animal alone.

faq.question: When is the next Fire Dog year?
faq.answer: 2066, sixty years later, when the five elements and twelve animals line up again; the table also has 1946.
